title: Wellness
description: Recovery board: is the body absorbing the training. Overnight recovery (sleep, HRV, resting HR) from core.sleep_session and mart.wellness_baseline, plus daytime load (stress, body battery, steps) from core.daily_wellness.

list.name: athlete_id
list.query: SELECT a.athlete_id AS __value, a.display_name AS __text FROM core.athlete a ORDER BY a.athlete_id
list.definition: SELECT a.athlete_id AS __value, a.display_name AS __text FROM core.athlete a ORDER BY a.athlete_id

target.rawSql: SELECT n.local_date::timestamp AS time, n.note AS text, n.kind AS tags FROM core.note n WHERE n.athlete_id = $athlete_id ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Sleep duration and stages
panels.description: core.sleep_session, one row per night keyed on wake_date (not the bedtime date). deep_s/light_s/rem_s/awake_s converted to hours and stacked, with all stage columns expected to be populated.

targets.rawSql: SELECT s.wake_date::timestamp AS time, s.deep_s / 3600.0 AS "Deep", s.light_s / 3600.0 AS "Light", s.rem_s / 3600.0 AS "REM", s.awake_s / 3600.0 AS "Awake" FROM core.sleep_session s WHERE s.athlete_id = $athlete_id AND $__timeFilter(s.wake_date) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Sleep score and respiration
panels.description: core.sleep_session.sleep_score (0-100, left axis) and avg_respiration (breaths/min, right axis), per night by wake_date. Both columns are expected to be populated on every night.

targets.rawSql: SELECT s.wake_date::timestamp AS time, s.sleep_score AS "Sleep score", s.avg_respiration AS "Avg respiration (brpm)" FROM core.sleep_session s WHERE s.athlete_id = $athlete_id AND $__timeFilter(s.wake_date) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: SpO2 overnight
panels.description: core.sleep_session.avg_spo2, percent, per night by wake_date. Missing nights are a Garmin collection gap, not a real drop -- gaps in the line are expected and are not a health signal.

targets.rawSql: SELECT s.wake_date::timestamp AS time, s.avg_spo2 AS "SpO2" FROM core.sleep_session s WHERE s.athlete_id = $athlete_id AND $__timeFilter(s.wake_date) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: HRV vs baseline
panels.description: Flagship recovery panel: mart.wellness_baseline.hrv_value (last-night HRV, ms) against hrv_baseline (rolling baseline, ms). HRV tracking near or above its baseline indicates good recovery; a sustained drop below baseline is the main early-warning signal on this dashboard.

targets.rawSql: SELECT b.local_date::timestamp AS time, b.hrv_value AS "HRV (ms)", b.hrv_baseline AS "HRV baseline (ms)" FROM mart.wellness_baseline b WHERE b.athlete_id = $athlete_id AND $__timeFilter(b.local_date) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: HRV deviation from baseline
panels.description: mart.wellness_baseline.hrv_dev_ratio * 100, as a percent, per day. Sign convention: hrv_dev_ratio = value / baseline - 1, so a NEGATIVE bar means HRV is BELOW baseline (the direction that matters for recovery) and a positive bar means HRV is above baseline. Zero line marks parity with baseline.

targets.rawSql: SELECT b.local_date::timestamp AS time, b.hrv_dev_ratio * 100 AS "HRV deviation" FROM mart.wellness_baseline b WHERE b.athlete_id = $athlete_id AND $__timeFilter(b.local_date) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Resting HR vs baseline
panels.description: mart.wellness_baseline.rhr_value and rhr_baseline (bpm, left axis) plus rhr_dev_bpm (bpm, right axis, bars) = value - baseline. Sign convention is the OPPOSITE of the HRV deviation panel next to it: here a POSITIVE bar means resting HR is ABOVE baseline, which is the bad direction (elevated resting HR usually signals incomplete recovery, illness, or accumulated fatigue).

targets.rawSql: SELECT b.local_date::timestamp AS time, b.rhr_value AS "Resting HR (bpm)", b.rhr_baseline AS "RHR baseline (bpm)", b.rhr_dev_bpm AS "RHR deviation (bpm)" FROM mart.wellness_baseline b WHERE b.athlete_id = $athlete_id AND $__timeFilter(b.local_date) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: HRV status (recent days)
panels.description: core.daily_wellness.hrv_status, Garmin's own text classification (e.g. balanced, unbalanced, low). Rendered as a table rather than a state-timeline: a state-timeline needs explicit value-color mappings for every text label Garmin may emit, which is fragile in schemaVersion 39 without a live database to enumerate the label set -- a table shows the raw text reliably regardless of which labels appear.

targets.rawSql: SELECT w.local_date AS "Date", w.hrv_status AS "HRV status" FROM core.daily_wellness w WHERE w.athlete_id = $athlete_id AND $__timeFilter(w.local_date) ORDER BY w.local_date DESC

panels.title: Body battery
panels.description: core.daily_wellness.body_battery_high and body_battery_low, per day, 0-100 scale. The gap between the two lines each day is the day's drain -- a wide gap means the day consumed most of the overnight charge.

targets.rawSql: SELECT w.local_date::timestamp AS time, w.body_battery_high AS "Body Battery high", w.body_battery_low AS "Body Battery low" FROM core.daily_wellness w WHERE w.athlete_id = $athlete_id AND $__timeFilter(w.local_date) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Average stress
panels.description: core.daily_wellness.avg_stress, Garmin's 0-100 daily stress score, per day.

targets.rawSql: SELECT w.local_date::timestamp AS time, w.avg_stress AS "Avg stress" FROM core.daily_wellness w WHERE w.athlete_id = $athlete_id AND $__timeFilter(w.local_date) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: VO2max (running)
panels.description: core.daily_wellness.vo2max_running, per day. Garmin's estimate updates in slow, infrequent steps rather than continuously -- read this as a coarse trend over weeks, not a precise daily measurement. No cycling VO2max panel is built here.

targets.rawSql: SELECT w.local_date::timestamp AS time, w.vo2max_running AS "VO2max running" FROM core.daily_wellness w WHERE w.athlete_id = $athlete_id AND $__timeFilter(w.local_date) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Daily steps, floors and intensity minutes
panels.description: core.daily_wellness.steps, floors, intensity_minutes, per day. Empty until the daily activity endpoints are added to the poller. The empty chart is a known collection gap, not a broken panel.

targets.rawSql: SELECT w.local_date::timestamp AS time, w.steps AS "Steps", w.floors AS "Floors", w.intensity_minutes AS "Intensity minutes" FROM core.daily_wellness w WHERE w.athlete_id = $athlete_id AND $__timeFilter(w.local_date) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Weight
panels.description: core.daily_wellness.weight_kg, per day, read directly from the column (never hardcoded). Empty until the daily activity endpoints are added to the poller. Kept here (empty) so the gap is visible and explained rather than hidden.

targets.rawSql: SELECT w.local_date::timestamp AS time, w.weight_kg AS "Weight" FROM core.daily_wellness w WHERE w.athlete_id = $athlete_id AND $__timeFilter(w.local_date) ORDER BY 1
